scope: Five shared surah-level source comparisons, linked to 23 verse keys; not 23 independent passage evaluations. Source-based review by ChatGPT; not an independent human review. Findings are evidenced examples, not an exhaustive apparatus of every variant.
method: User-directed complete-source fidelity grading: compare the supplied English against the entire stored Arabic commentary unit. Deduct for omitted material even when the English is deliberately abridged; separately deduct for meaning changes/additions and damaged English text. Withhold only when a trustworthy Arabic comparison unit cannot be identified. No theology or historical truth is graded. Scores are reasoned editorial assessments, not measured percentages of correct words. No source text is rewritten.

reviews.name: An-Nasr
reviews.accurate: The retained passages preserve Ibn Abbas’s explanation that the surah announces the approaching end of the Prophet’s life, the prayers reported by Aishah, the conquest of Makkah, and Jabir’s report about people entering and leaving the religion in crowds.
reviews.omitted: The abridged English omits the reports involving Fatimah and the people of Yemen, Abu Said’s exchange with Marwan, and the extended discussion of the eight-rakah conquest prayer and its manner of salutation. These are coverage omissions, not proof that the retained English reverses the source.
reviews.mistranslated: The Arabic book title السيرة is printed in the English as “As-Surah”; “al-Sirah” is the corresponding title. The English also repeats “He (Ibn `Abbas)” in the opening paragraph. No broader verdict about every retained sentence is implied.
reviews.concerns: The English is identified in the database as an abridged edition. Different language lengths are not a measure of translation accuracy. Arabic is missing at 110:3; the contextual Arabic block is stored at 110:1–2.
reviews.verdict: 6/10 against the full stored Arabic commentary. Omissions—including deliberate abridgment—reduce the grade. Deductions from 10: coverage 3.5; changed meaning 0; English text integrity 0.5. This is a shared surah-block score, not a measured percentage of correctly translated words.

anchors.ar: من صلاة النبي ﷺ يوم فتح مكة وقت الضحى ثماني ركعات

coverage.reason: Substantial unique reports and the extended conquest-prayer discussion are absent; retained central interpretations remain recognizable.

meaning.reason: No separate meaning penalty is assigned for the documented retained examples.

text_integrity.reason: The book-title transcription and duplicated attribution receive a small text-integrity deduction.

reviews.name: Al-Masad
reviews.accurate: The English retains the opening warning to Quraysh, Abu Lahab’s hostility, the interpretation of kasab as children, Umm Jamil’s support for her husband, and the account in which she does not see the Prophet.
reviews.omitted: The English omits the Ibn Ishaq report about approaching the tribes; several interpretations of carrying wood and masad; the second account of Umm Jamil with al-Bazzar’s chain assessment; and the concluding argument that the couple’s failure to believe is evidence of prophethood.
reviews.mistranslated: In the retained Umm Jamil verse, “مذمما أبينا ودينه قلينا وأمره عصينا” expresses rejection of the disparagingly named person, hatred of his religion, and disobedience to his command. The supplied English instead says “He criticizes our father” and “his command is to disobey us,” changing the actors and sense. In another retained report, “أزفر القربة” refers to carrying a waterskin, whereas the English says “the strongest blower of the flute (for music).” These are substantive lexical/semantic problems, separate from abridgment.
reviews.concerns: The Arabic kunya is أبو عتبة, while the English prints Abu `Utaybah. This is a textual name discrepancy; checking editions is needed before assigning its origin to the translator.
reviews.verdict: 5/10 against the full stored Arabic commentary. Omissions—including deliberate abridgment—reduce the grade. Deductions from 10: coverage 3; changed meaning 2; English text integrity 0. This is a shared surah-block score, not a measured percentage of correctly translated words.

anchors.ar: مذمما أبينا ودينه قلينا وأمره عصينا

coverage.reason: Multiple interpretations, the second narrative with source assessment, and the concluding argument are absent.

meaning.reason: The Umm Jamil verse changes the actors and meaning; the waterskin/flute rendering is a substantive lexical error. The name discrepancy is included in this category.

text_integrity.reason: No additional integrity penalty: the named discrepancies are already counted as meaning issues.

reviews.name: Al-Ikhlas
reviews.accurate: The English retains the main teaching of divine oneness, several virtue reports, Ibn Abbas’s explanation of al-Samad as the perfect master depended upon by creation, and the denial of offspring, parent, or spouse.
reviews.omitted: Many virtue reports and their chain assessments are omitted. The Arabic discussion of al-Samad includes “الذي لا جوف له,” the report “نور يتلألأ,” and Ibn Kathir’s distinction between raised and stopped attribution; these do not appear in the supplied English. These are missing scholarly material, not automatically mistranslations of retained material.
reviews.mistranslated: The report beginning “أصابنا طش وظلمة” concerns drizzle/light rain and darkness, but the supplied English says “We became thirsty and it had become dark.” At the end, “وليس أول الخلق بأهون علي من إعادته” says that initial creation is not easier for God than recreation; “the re-creation of him is easier than his original creation” changes that formulation to a positive comparative. The latter should be marked a strengthened paraphrase, not a denial of resurrection.
reviews.concerns: The English greatest-name supplication report visibly stops mid-Arabic quotation at “الذي إذ” and jumps to the next heading without completing or translating the response. The opening “So Allah revealed” also runs into the basmalah rather than the surah quotation given there in Arabic. These are stored-text defects; this review does not establish whether they originated in the edition or ingestion.
reviews.verdict: 4.5/10 against the full stored Arabic commentary. Omissions—including deliberate abridgment—reduce the grade. Deductions from 10: coverage 3.5; changed meaning 1; English text integrity 1. This is a shared surah-block score, not a measured percentage of correctly translated words.

reviews.name: Al-Falaq
reviews.accurate: The English preserves the opening report that Ibn Masud did not write the two refuge surahs in his mushaf, Ubayy’s response, selected virtue reports, the dawn interpretation, several explanations of ghasiq, and the report that the Prophet imagined relations with his wives that had not occurred.
reviews.omitted: The Arabic includes additional reports that Ibn Masud erased the two surahs and said they were not from the Book of God, followed by Ibn Kathir’s tentative explanations and suggestion of a later return to the community’s view. The English omits those reports and that reconciliation. It also omits alternative explanations of al-falaq with source criticism, and the final al-Thalabi narrative together with Ibn Kathir’s warning that it lacks an isnad and contains strongly objectionable details. Omitting both a report and its criticism is a coverage gap, not evidence that the English endorses the omitted report.
reviews.mistranslated: The Arabic introduction says “وهما مدنيتان” (the two are Medinan), whereas the English heading says “Which was revealed in Makkah.” This is an explicit discrepancy between the supplied texts; it does not decide the historical revelation-location dispute. For Abu Said’s protection report, the Arabic gives al-Tirmidhi’s assessment as “حديث حسن,” while the English prints “Hasan Sahih,” strengthening the stated grading.
reviews.concerns: No motive for abridgment is inferred. The English explicitly presents an abridged edition. Arabic is missing at 113:5; the contextual Arabic block is stored at 113:1–4. The introductory Arabic block concerns both refuge surahs, not exclusively verse 113:1.
reviews.verdict: 4.5/10 against the full stored Arabic commentary. Omissions—including deliberate abridgment—reduce the grade. Deductions from 10: coverage 4; changed meaning 1.5; English text integrity 0. This is a shared surah-block score, not a measured percentage of correctly translated words.

coverage.reason: The missing Ibn Masud reports and reconciliation, alternative interpretations with criticism, and final narrative with its warning materially narrow the source presentation.

meaning.reason: The revelation-location heading contradicts the supplied Arabic, and Hasan becomes Hasan Sahih in the reported grading.

text_integrity.reason: No additional integrity penalty is needed for the cited findings.

reviews.name: An-Nas
reviews.accurate: The English retains lordship, sovereignty and divinity; the accompanying devil report; Safiyyah’s visit; the interpretations of the withdrawing whisperer; the question whether al-nas includes jinn; and the final report about unwanted thoughts.
reviews.omitted: The English omits the Abu Yala report with Ibn Kathir’s “غريب” comment, the stumbled-donkey report and its chain assessment, the Abu Hurayrah mosque report, and the extended Abu Dharr dialogue. Both texts reach the final Ibn Abbas report, but these internal omissions prevent treating them as a complete translation pair.
reviews.mistranslated: The Arabic explains the inclusion of jinn under the label al-nas with “تغليبا” (linguistic predominance: using a dominant group’s name for a mixed group). The English renders this as “in most cases,” turning a linguistic explanation into a frequency claim.
reviews.concerns: Arabic at 114:1 is only a 93-character introduction; it is not the full counterpart of the English. Full contextual Arabic is stored at 114:2–5, while Arabic at 114:6 is missing. No full Arabic entry has been silently substituted at those verse keys.
reviews.verdict: 6/10 against the full stored Arabic commentary. Omissions—including deliberate abridgment—reduce the grade. Deductions from 10: coverage 3; changed meaning 1; English text integrity 0. This is a shared surah-block score, not a measured percentage of correctly translated words.

coverage.meaning: Missing source content, including deliberate abridgment. Weight unique interpretation and critical qualifications more than repeated transmission routes.

meaning.meaning: Changed meaning, additions, names, negation, or strengthened/softened claims in overlapping passages.

text_integrity.meaning: Cut-off quotations, transcription defects, or damaged English text. Do not count the same defect again under coverage.

rubric.calculation: 10 minus the three stated deductions. Category penalties are qualitative judgments tied to cited examples; they are not character-count ratios or an exhaustive count of propositions.
rubric.source_unit: Whole shared surah commentary; repeated verse links carry the same unit score.
